title: the table's upgrade row declares one flag group where its own declared v2 twin parses four -- an undeclared flag cannot regress, because nothing compares it
body:
The table's `upgrade` row carries `disposition: keep`, names its own v2 twin as `bin/intent_upgrade`, and declares exactly one flag group: `["--help","-h"]`.

THE TWIN IT NAMES PARSES THREE MORE. `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/extract_flags.sh` -- already in that directory, already correct -- reads `bin/intent_upgrade` as parsing `--backup-dir --dry-run --help --no-backup -h`.

STATE OF EACH, DRIVEN:

- `--no-backup` -- absent from the table; parsed by the twin at `bin/intent_upgrade:69`; asserted GREEN five times by the bats estate (`tests/unit/intent_upgrade_dispatcher.bats:12` and four more); v3 REFUSES it today: `error: unexpected argument '--no-backup' found`, rc=1.
- `--backup-dir` -- absent from the ENTIRE table, not merely from this row.
- `--dry-run` -- declared on six other rows (`st`, `bootstrap`, `organize`, `claude skills`, `treeindex`, `st_zero`) and not on this one.

THE FRAMING THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT "THREE FLAGS ARE MISSING". **An undeclared flag cannot regress, because nothing compares it.** v3 refuses `--no-backup` right now and no instrument said a word -- not `surface_check.sh`, which compares the binary to the table and therefore agrees with the table about what the table contains; not `coverage_map.sh`, which joins at FAMILY granularity and sees `upgrade` covered; not the two generators, which render what they are handed. The declaration is what makes a difference detectable, so an omitted row removes the flag from every instrument's reach at once. That is why this is filed as a table defect rather than as a v3 behaviour question: whether v3 SHOULD accept `--no-backup` is a design call, and it cannot even be asked while the row does not name it.

A THIRD HOME EXISTS AND ALREADY HAD THE ANSWER -- see the companion issue on the inventory re-derivation gap. `intent/st/ST0056/parity/cmd-upgrade.md`, generated by `gen_inventory.sh`, declares `--backup-dir` and `--no-backup` in its flag table. So this was never nobody-measured: three derivations of what flags `upgrade` has exist, they disagree, and the SSOT is the one that did not derive itself.

FOUND BY `suite_vs_table_flags_check.sh` (`32c7ad52`) on the `--no-backup` axis; `--backup-dir` and the `--dry-run` asymmetry came from vc driving the row's own declared twin by hand, which is the adjacent axis that instrument names in its header and does not implement.

REMEDY: decide each of the three and declare the decision on the row -- a flag v3 drops is a `disposition` the table can carry, and an undeclared flag is not. Size S.
